Section 1
The Guardian issued corrections to several stories published on 25 August. It clarified that the new pet‑theft legislation, which makes dog or cat abduction a specific crime, only covers England and Northern Ireland, not the whole United Kingdom.

Section 2
It also amended the description of Eileen Burbidge’s role at Fertifa, noting she is the executive director while the company’s founders are Tony Chen and Nick Kuan. In the Q&A with Juliet Stevenson, the director’s name was corrected from “Lowther” to Alex Lawther, and the film Bend It Like Beckham’s central family was identified as Sikh rather than Muslim.

***
Section 3
Regarding Venetia Stanley’s connection to Herbert Asquith, the paper noted that her father, the fourth Baron Stanley of Alderley, did not convert to Islam; the conversion was made by her uncle, the third Baron Stanley. Additionally, a list of other recently updated articles was provided, ranging from the arrest of Telegram founder Pavel Durov at a French airport to features on royal servants, papal comments on England’s football tactics, Britain’s sci‑tech potential, the Salvator Mundi controversy, and a final note on summer wines.

Section 4
* Readers wishing to contact the Readers’ Editor can write to the Observer at York Way, London N1 9GU, email observer.readers@observer.co.uk, or call 020 3353 4736.
* The corrections aim to ensure factual accuracy across the publication’s coverage.

P.P.S Thank you for reading the clarified version of the Guardian’s August 25 corrections.
